slides.heading: Three Number Sum
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Three Number Sum, a medium arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: All triplets of distinct integers summing to target, each triplet ascending and the list sorted.
Sort then sweep with two pointers.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. All triplets of distinct integers summing to target, each triplet ascending and the list sorted. Sort then sweep with two pointers.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Fix one number, then find pairs in the sorted remainder with two pointers.
slides.narration: Fix one number, then find pairs in the sorted remainder with two pointers.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: three nested loops → O(n³)
Fix one + hash set for the pair → O(n²) time, O(n) space
Sort + fix one + two pointers → O(n²), O(1) extra
slides.narration: Three nested loops are cubic. Fixing one number and using a hash set for the other two is quadratic with extra memory. Sorting, fixing one number, and closing in with two pointers is quadratic with constant extra space, and naturally sorted output.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each index, set left and right pointers after it
3. Move them based on the current sum
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort the array. Second, for each index, set left and right pointers after it. Third, move them based on the current sum. Fourth, record exact matches.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: sum -2 < 0 → L++
slides.narration: With -8 fixed, -6 plus 12 gives -2. Too small, so move left forward.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: sum 5 > 0 → R−−
slides.narration: With -8 fixed, 1 plus 12 gives 5. Too big, so move right back.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: sum -1 < 0 → L++
slides.narration: With -8 fixed, 1 plus 6 gives -1. Too small, so move left forward.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: sum 0 = 0 ✓
slides.narration: With -8 fixed, 2 plus 6 gives 0. That's a match; record it and move both pointers.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: sum 0 = 0 ✓
slides.narration: With -8 fixed, 3 plus 5 gives 0. That's a match; record it and move both pointers.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: sum 7 > 0 → R−−
slides.narration: With -6 fixed, 1 plus 12 gives 7. Too big, so move right back.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We sort, then for each index i set l right after it and r at the end. We compute the sum; on a match we record and move both, otherwise move l forward if too small or r back if too big.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n squared. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Distinct values here; with duplicates, skip repeats
Move both pointers after a match
slides.narration: This problem has distinct values. With duplicates you'd skip repeated values to avoid duplicate triplets. After a match, move both pointers.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Mention that this generalises to k-sum, and a common follow-up is the closest three-sum.

bullets: Fix one number, then find pairs in the sorted remainder with two pointers.
